idiom_name: object literals with a kind/type discriminator + one recursive eval function
implementation_notes: The JavaScript default is data, not classes: AST nodes are object literals with a discriminating kind field, and one recursive eval function switches on it and recurses. There is no type system to check completeness, so keep an explicit default branch that throws a descriptive error and test each node kind. Representing the same node with different key sets is the pitfall to avoid: keep one shape per kind so the engine keeps a monomorphic access path.
pitfalls: No exhaustiveness and no types: a new kind fails at run time on the first evaluation, so the default branch must throw and each kind needs a test.
Objects whose shape changes after construction (fields added later) de-optimise property access in V8; build nodes with every field present from the start.
Untagged or duplicated discriminators break the switch silently - two kinds sharing a value will evaluate with the wrong rule.

variants.name: Class per grammar rule with an interpret method
variants.idiom_name: abstract Expr base class + subclass per rule overriding interpret(context)
variants.implementation_notes: The GoF form in JavaScript: an abstract base class declaring interpret, one subclass per grammar rule, recursion through child fields. It is the right choice when node classes are the extension point (a plugin returns new node types) or when the interpreter object itself must be swappable, and it gives natural places for constructor validation. The cost is a dynamic method call per node and instance allocation, which the tagged-object switch avoids.
pitfalls: A subclass that forgets the override inherits the base throw, so the failure surfaces only when that node is evaluated - the deepest, least convenient point.
Instances are heavier than plain objects and each class adds a prototype: for large trees the allocation and call overhead is measurable.
Prototype methods are enumerable-prone in old code and class fields initialise in declaration order, so a subclass constructor that calls interpret before children are set sees undefined.
